title: The filtered colimit of a system of categories; finite diagrams and morphisms come from a stage
statement: Let $\mathcal J$ be a small filtered category, for $j\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal J)$ let $\mathcal C_j$ be a category whose objects and morphisms form sets, and for $\phi:j\to j'$ let $v_\phi:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_{j'}$ be a functor, with $v_{\mathrm{id}_j}=\mathrm{id}$ and $v_{\psi\circ\phi}=v_\psi\circ v_\phi$ (equality of functors). Let $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal J}\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$ and $\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C)=\varinjlim_{\mathcal J}\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C_j)$ (filtered colimits of sets along the maps induced by the $v_\phi$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), with coprojections written $v_j$, and let source, target, identities and composition of $\mathcal C$ be induced by those of the $\mathcal C_j$: $v_j(\beta)\circ v_j(\alpha)=v_j(\beta\circ\alpha)$ for composable $\alpha,\beta$ in $\mathcal C_j$. Then: (1) these operations are well defined and make $\mathcal C$ a category whose objects and morphisms form sets, and $v_j:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C$ is a functor with $v_{j'}\circ v_\phi=v_j$ for $\phi:j\to j'$. (2) Every finite diagram of $\mathcal C$ comes from a stage: given finitely many objects $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and morphisms $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_m$ of $\mathcal C$ together with finitely many relations among them, each of the form $\mathrm{source}(\alpha_p)=X_q$, $\mathrm{target}(\alpha_p)=X_q$, $\alpha_p\circ\alpha_q=\alpha_r$ or $\alpha_p=\mathrm{id}_{X_q}$, there are $j$, objects $X_{q,j}$ and morphisms $\alpha_{p,j}$ of $\mathcal C_j$ with $v_j(X_{q,j})=X_q$, $v_j(\alpha_{p,j})=\alpha_p$ satisfying the same relations in $\mathcal C_j$; moreover, two such lifts at stages $j$, $j'$ become equal at some stage $k$ after applying $v_\phi$, $v_{\phi'}$ for suitable $\phi:j\to k$, $\phi':j'\to k$. In particular every functor $D:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ from a finite category is $v_j\circ D_j$ for some $j$ and some functor $D_j:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_j$. (3) For $j\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal J)$ and $X,Y\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_j)$, the maps $\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_{j'}}(v_\phi X,v_\phi Y)\to\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(v_jX,v_jY)$, $\beta\mapsto v_{j'}(\beta)$, for $\phi:j\to j'$ in the (filtered) category $j/\mathcal J$ of morphisms out of $j$, induce a bijection $\varinjlim_{\phi:j\to j'}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C_{j'}}(v_\phi X,v_\phi Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(v_jX,v_jY)$. (4) A morphism of $\mathcal C$ is an isomorphism if and only if it is $v_j(\gamma)$ for some $j$ and some isomorphism $\gamma$ of $\mathcal C_j$.
